title: Sort a roster with one cached, chained comparator

blocks.text: `Comparator` is a functional interface with composition built in: `comparing`, `thenComparingInt`, `thenComparing`, `reversed` and `nullsFirst`. A comparator that is used again and again belongs in a `private static final` constant, so the lambda is built once.
`Person` is the record `Person(String name, int age, String department)`. Write three static methods of `Roster`:

items: `Comparator<Person> byDepartmentAgeName()` orders by department, then by age, then by name, and returns the same comparator object every time.
`Comparator<Person> oldestFirst()` orders by age, oldest first.
`List<Person> sorted(List<Person> people)` returns a new list in `byDepartmentAgeName()` order, leaving `people` untouched; `null` entries go first.

blocks.text: Mind the tie on both department and age, a `null` in the list, and how many comparators you make.

cases.says: People sort by department, then age, then name, and oldestFirst puts the oldest first.
When department and age tie, the name decides the order.
sorted puts null entries first instead of throwing.
The comparator is kept in a constant and reused, not rebuilt on every call.
sorted returns a new list and leaves the caller's list in its original order.

concepts: A lambda that is reused, such as a comparator, is kept in a static final constant rather than rebuilt.
Comparators chain with thenComparing, flip with reversed and admit nulls with nullsFirst.
